sources.tag: read: notes on stress
sources.note: SIL has no language page and no publication for zpp; the held SIL OAI harvest has no record coded [zpp]. The 'Zimatlán' items (Olson, Diccionario/Gramática/Cuentos zapoteco de Zimatlán) are all Santa Inés Yatzechi [zpn], Southeastern Zimatlán, not El Alto.

sources.citation: LINGMEX, Bibliografía lingüística de México desde 1970 (El Colegio de México), full record dumps for language categories 'Zapoteco' (720 records) and 'Zapotecas' (48 records), queried 2026-09-17
sources.tag: read: notes on stress
sources.note: No record mentions San Pedro el Alto, San Antonino/San Antonio el Alto, San Andrés el Alto, Zimatlán (other than Santa Inés Yatzechi works) or Coyachilla: no Mexican thesis, article or grammar on this variety is registered.

sources.citation: Sicoli, Mark A. 2021. Deliberate Decisions and Unintended Consequences: Ratifying Nonspeakers through Code Alternation in Child-Directed Speech. In Anna M. Babel & Mark A. Sicoli (eds.), Contact, Structure, and Change: A Festschrift in Honor of Sarah G. Thomason, 1-34. Ann Arbor: Michigan Publishing (Maize Books). doi:10.3998/mpub.11616118 (open access, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0).
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on El Alto prosody. For Lachixío it mentions falsetto/high pitch = respect and low pitch/breathy = authority voice registers (p. 7) and cites Sicoli 2007 for tone. For El Alto it gives only survey scope and vitality: 'I worked with one of the last fluent speakers from San Andres el Alto in 1998, only older people in San Pedro can speak the language today, and no one younger than about fifty years currently speaks the language in San Antonino.'

sources.citation: Ethnologue 18th ed. (2015), entry 'Zapotec, El Alto' [zpp] (Internet Archive copy of ethnologue.com/language/zpp)
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Nothing. Alternate names South Central Zimatlan Zapotec, Zapoteco de San Pedro el Alto; 900 speakers (1990 census), no monolinguals; San Andrés el Alto, San Antonino el Alto, San Pedro el Alto; 'None known [dialects]. 20% intelligibility of Totomachapan (most similar)'; 'Unwritten'. (Saved file is the the Internet Archive HTML.)

sources.citation: Egland, Steven T., Doris A. Bartholomew & Saúl Cruz Ramos. 1978 [1983]. La inteligibilidad interdialectal en México: Resultados de algunos sondeos. México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. 38 pp. (Zapotec section pp. 66-78)
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Intelligibility survey only. p. 66 sets up grouping '6. S. Pedro el Alto, Zimatlán -20- (en Río Dulce) / S. Antonio el Alto, Zim. 94' with footnote 'Río Dulce fue sólo punto de referencia. Totomachapan obtuvo (0)% en S. Pedro el Alto.'; p. 78: 'El zapoteco de S. Pedro el Alto parece incluir a S. Andrés el Alto.' plus the intelligibility matrix (S. Pedro el Alto row). Scan with no text layer; scanned (eng, 200 dpi) and the two key pages checked against the page images. This is the origin of Ethnologue's zpp unit; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid elal1235 'El Alto Zapotec' (references tab / JSON record)
